extraction.name: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB)
extraction.description: A benchmark of text embeddings spanning 8 tasks, 58 datasets and 112 languages. Tasks include bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity and summarization. MTEB provides an open-source evaluation framework and a public leaderboard.
extraction.creator: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, Nils Reimers
extraction.inLanguage: 112 languages; 10 datasets are multilingual. Retrieval and clustering datasets are English-only.
extraction.citeAs: Niklas Muennighoff, Nouamane Tazi, Loïc Magne, and Nils Reimers. MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. arXiv:2210.07316v3, 19 March 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MTEB unifies existing datasets from different text embedding tasks, including SemEval STS datasets and all publicly available BEIR retrieval datasets. Custom scientific-paper clustering datasets were collected using the public arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv APIs. RedditClusteringP2P and StackExchangeClusteringP2P were created using existing post datasets. For scientific clustering datasets, subsets of labels were selected and articles sampled from those labels to produce splits with varying cluster numbers and sizes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sources include existing SemEval and BEIR datasets; paper titles, abstracts and categories from the arXiv and bioRxiv/medRxiv public APIs; Reddit posts from https://huggingface.co/datasets/sentence-transformers/reddit-title-body; StackExchange posts from https://huggingface.co/datasets/flax-sentence-embeddings/stackexchange_title_body_jsonl; and the 20 Newsgroups dataset. Other constituent datasets contain Amazon customer reviews, online banking queries, Twitter messages, IMDb movie reviews, Amazon Alexa utterances, MTOP sentences, Civil Comments comments, community questions, news article titles, translated sentence pairs, biomedical sentence pairs and human-written or machine-generated summaries.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For custom scientific-paper clustering datasets, sentence-to-sentence inputs use paper titles, while paragraph-to-paragraph inputs concatenate titles and abstracts. RedditClusteringP2P and StackExchangeClusteringP2P concatenate post titles and bodies. Scientific-paper clustering splits use main categories, secondary categories within a main category, or secondary categories across all main categories. Subsets of labels and articles are sampled to vary cluster numbers and sizes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Datasets are organized into sentence-to-sentence, paragraph-to-paragraph and sentence-to-paragraph settings. MTEB imposes no input-length limit and leaves truncation to individual models. Scientific-paper clustering inputs are prepared as titles alone or concatenated titles and abstracts; paragraph-level Reddit and StackExchange inputs concatenate titles and posts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Existing dataset annotations are reused. Custom scientific clustering labels derive from categories assigned to papers by humans. bioRxiv and medRxiv papers have unique categories; for arXiv papers with multiple categories, only the first is used. Reddit clustering uses subreddits, and StackExchange title clustering uses StackExchange sites. Classification annotations include counterfactual status, sentiment, review scores, banking intents, emotions, Alexa intents or scenarios, MTOP domains or intents, and toxicity. Pair classification uses duplicate or paraphrase labels. BUCC and Tatoeba provide annotated translation pairs. AskUbuntu includes manual similar/dissimilar question-pair annotations. STS labels are continuous similarity scores from 0 to 5. SummEval includes human assessments of machine-generated summaries.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For arXiv papers assigned multiple categories, only the first category is retained for clustering labels. Categories are mapped into main-category and secondary-category clustering settings.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MTEB uses dataset-level and software-level versioning to support reproducibility. The authors welcome community contributions of datasets, tasks and metrics through pull requests, and leaderboard additions through an automatic submission format. New datasets for existing tasks can be added through a single file specifying the task and Hugging Face dataset name. The authors hope to add datasets to underrepresented tasks such as summarization and pair classification. No update schedule or deprecation policy is stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: A RedditClusteringP2P example contains self-reported age and gender ('22f'), ADHD diagnosis, medication use, medication affordability and lack of insurance. These appear within an example post rather than as separately described structured attributes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors aim to make selection of appropriate embedding models easier for research and industry applications and reduce blind reuse of models across different tasks. Open-source evaluation and a public leaderboard are intended to simplify future embedding research and provide a foundation for improving text embeddings.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Overall benchmark averages are biased toward tasks with more datasets, notably retrieval, classification and clustering; summarization has only one dataset. Some evaluated models have training-data overlap with MTEB datasets, including parts of SciDocsRR. The authors state that controlling for contamination is challenging and ignore training-data overlap in MTEB scores.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Very long documents are absent; the longest datasets contain only a few hundred words. Tasks have unequal numbers of datasets. Multilingual datasets cover classification, STS and bitext mining, while retrieval and clustering are English-only, limiting comprehensive evaluation of multilingual retrieval models. MTEB contains no code datasets and focuses solely on natural-language applications rather than evaluating text embeddings as inputs to other modalities. Several datasets share corpora or have similar sentence-level and paragraph-level variants. Training-data contamination is not controlled in benchmark scores.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and benchmarking of text embedding models across bitext mining, classification, clustering, pair classification, reranking, retrieval, semantic textual similarity and summarization. The benchmark supports model selection, comparisons of performance, speed and embedding storage requirements, multilingual evaluation and future embedding research. The paper evaluates test splits except for MSMARCO, where the development split is used. Classification trains a logistic regression classifier on training-set embeddings and evaluates it on test-set embeddings.
